name: Dennis Wetzig
headline: Running PIXRAY & loving it.
summary:
I do not read my LinkedIn messages regularly. Please send an email instead. 

At PIXRAY I am proud to serve news agencies, photo agencies and other owners of visual content to help them develop sustainable copyright enforcement businesses that are in line with their culture and values. I love to help my customers future-proof their companies and give them an innovative edge in a market that is under attack from many sides.

As a founder I had to learn that being a great leader requires more than being a technology expert. My openness to reflect on the way I lead and my desire to learn have allowed me to develop the skills required to run an effective organization. Understanding that leaders are made, not born, was key for me.

I wrote my first few lines of code on a Commodore VC20 computer as a child when I was barely able to read and write. As simple as those lines of code were, the powerful feeling of being able to build something that works remained with me ever since. 

My early experimentation kicked off a learning path in which I became a fully self-taught coding, TCP/IP networking and UNIX expert at a very young age. I contributed to international software projects and was hired as a coder by the world’s largest web portal at the time, Lycos, as a 17-year-old teenager while still in high-school.

As a CEO I strive to create a results-driven culture based on intellectual honesty, first principles thinking, trust, ownership and the willingness to learn.

I run my company in a way that makes success in business and raising a family compatible for my team because I know that this has a great positive impact on our culture and productivity.

My greatest asset today is range. As a founder I am exposed to a broad variety of challenges that give me opportunities to learn. I am also an avid reader, and I am constantly trying to expose myself to new topics, concepts and views. I am able to transfer patterns from one domain to another and can synthesize knowledge from various disciplines into new approaches. This allows me to see consequences and solutions that others don’t see. I am able to quickly identify and answer the make-or-break questions involved in a new endeavor.

positions.title: Advisory Board Member
positions.description: In 2019 I was asked to join the advisory board of diIT, a MES software company for the wire-harness industry. I consult diIT's management and owners, Schleuniger Group, in strategic direction-setting and technical decisions.

positions.title: Co-Founder & CEO
positions.description:
We drive sustainable copyright enforcement business models. Customers on three continents generate hundreds of thousands of dollars in monthly revenue with our platform. Now we set out to change the industry by introducing fairlicensing.com, a SaaS solution to support agencies to run copyright enforcement as an in-house sales process. Full control. No middleman. 

I co-founded PIXRAY and run the company as its CEO. I am proud of the company culture we built. It allows us to tackle massive technological challenges, deliver great products and services and help our customers succeed in an ever changing environment.

positions.title: Lecturer on Financial Business Modelling and Business Model Generation
positions.company: Center for Digital Technology and Management (CDTM)
positions.description: I taught students at the Center for Digital Technology and Management (CDTM), an Honors Degree Program of the Elite Network of Bavaria offered by LMU and TU Munich, in Financial Business Modelling and Business Model Generation. I had the opportunity to pass on some hard-won knowledge and learn from the students myself. Also it felt good to give something back to CDTM, which was a defining experience for myself as a student.

positions.title: Co-Founder & Managing Director
positions.description: Created a cloud storage and backup solution for photography before "cloud" was a thing. We secured seed funding and ran a small product development team. We pitched to leading VCs in Germany. They did not think that storing personal data in the cloud was ever going to happen and the company failed.

positions.title: Technical Director
positions.description: At age 21, I joined my biggest eViato client's business as a Technical Director. At MindMatics, based on eViato software, I helped run some of the highest-volume mobile messaging applications, like the international votings for Eurovision Song Contest, viewed by more than 120 million people worldwide, or mobile interactions for nation wide prime time shows on NBC together with our New York City office.

positions.title: Founder & CEO
positions.description: At 19, I founded my first company eViato and created a massively scalable server software that enabled customers to directly connect to mobile messaging service centers at mobile network operators for high-throughput mobile messaging applications. I sold licenses for tens of thousands of Euros each. The software I created built the backbone of my clients' businesses and is still in use today.

positions.title: Software Developer
positions.description: When I was 17, I approached the CTO of Lycos Europe, a subsidiary of US search giant lycos.com in cooperation with Bertelsmann, and was hired as an expert coder. I was their third employee in the European tech team. Lycos was the biggest internet portal in the world at the time. I started of by developing system management and monitoring software for the Lycos and Tripod (a Lycos subsidiary) platforms. Later I developed and operated mobile messaging products for the Lycos platform, earning Lycos significant advertising revenues. During my time with Lycos the company carried out an IPO and grew to more than 900 employees.

positions.title: Networking Software Developer
positions.description: While I was still a kid in high-school, CSI consulting asked me to join them as a networking software development expert in a complex software development project for one of their clients, a leading anti virus software company based in Ireland. I implemented a full TCP/IP based communication stack to connect the client's infrastructure to a credit card validation system over the internet. I implemented the full networking stack based on extensive protocol documentation.
